research_basis: brief-only discovery, before one-shot exact-plan reveal
access_batch_note: UTC values are clock observations immediately following batches in which pages were opened; browser does not expose each HTTP request timestamp.

sources.title: Slint invoke_from_event_loop
sources.observed_operation: Opened pinned docs.rs API page; reviewed signature and thread/event-loop description.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Thread-safe call from any thread; queued closure executes on thread that started event loop; captures must satisfy Send + 'static; non-Send work instead uses spawn_local.
sources.applicability: UI integration only; keeps worker result application on Slint event-loop thread; does not schedule or cancel parsing.

sources.title: Tokio spawn_blocking
sources.locator: Description, abort, shutdown, and CPU-bound guidance; lines 31-48
sources.observed_operation: Opened pinned docs.rs API page; reviewed bounded-worker, CPU, abort, and shutdown statements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Pool upper limit is Builder-configured and very large by default; CPU tasks should use semaphore/other bound; started blocking tasks cannot be aborted; shutdown_timeout stops waiting but does not cancel; intended for bounded operations.
sources.applicability: Relevant if project uses Tokio; shows why async abort is insufficient for untrusted blocking decoders and why concurrency must be explicit.

sources.title: Tokio bounded mpsc channel
sources.observed_operation: Opened docs.rs latest page and observed its crate header as Tokio 1.53.2; bounded channel docs reviewed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: buffer capacity must be at least one; buffer-full sends wait; FIFO preserves send order; one receiver. This provides backpressure but no priority lanes.
sources.applicability: Useful bounded message transport option; do not block the UI on a full channel; dispatcher must own lane policy.

sources.title: Rust sync_channel
sources.version_or_commit: Rust std 1.99.0 documentation; API stable since 1.0.0
sources.observed_operation: Opened current standard-library documentation and reviewed bounded buffer semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fixed-size FIFO buffer; sends block when full; zero bound is rendezvous. Nonblocking try_send is available through sender API but not part of the cited page.
sources.applicability: Runtime-independent transport alternative; scheduler should reject/defer admission rather than block UI when capacity is full.

sources.title: Rust std::process::Child
sources.version_or_commit: Rust std 1.99.0 documentation; Child/kill/wait stable since 1.0.0
sources.observed_operation: Opened current std documentation; inspected Child lifetime, kill, wait, and try_wait sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Dropping Child does not kill or wait; caller must reap. kill forces the direct child to exit (SIGKILL on Unix). Nightly-only process-group kill API is not a stable fallback.
sources.applicability: Use explicit child supervisor with kill and reap; separate platform-specific process-tree handling is needed.

sources.title: Windows Job Objects
sources.version_or_commit: Current Win32 documentation; version conditions stated in page
sources.locator: Managing processes, limits, close behavior, process-tree caveats; lines 31-87, 90-93
sources.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn platform page; reviewed process membership, limits, breakaway, and kill-on-close behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Job groups can be terminated and resource limits applied; ordinary CreateProcess children join by default; breakaway can remove descendants; nested jobs added Windows 8/Server 2012, older systems differ; security limits set per process on Vista+.
sources.applicability: Windows process-tree cleanup/resource management option for child handlers; not itself a complete sandbox/security boundary.

sources.title: Freedesktop Thumbnail Managing Standard
sources.locator: Thumbnail saving and modification detection; §6-7, lines 174-185, 212-241, 261-278
sources.observed_operation: Opened current single-page specification; verified version history, cache-key and metadata rules, atomic-save recipe, and stale checks.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Global thumbnail must carry canonical URI and MTime; size should be checked if present; mtime is seconds resolution; temporary file then rename is specified for complete-or-absent publication; mtime alone can collide and be insufficient.
sources.applicability: Local cache precedent only; borrow atomic publication and metadata checks, but use app-specific content/profile/handler version identity and stronger revision semantics.

sources.title: GNOME GnomeDesktopThumbnailFactory
sources.version_or_commit: gnome-desktop3 manual; exact manual release not stated; factory since 2.2
sources.observed_operation: Opened official GNOME API manual; reviewed helper selection, fallback, size limits, URI/mtime cache, failed cache, and main-thread/blocking annotations.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: MIME registrations select external helpers; helper writes output before exit and signals failure via nonzero exit; fallback gdk-pixbuf may run; normal/large dimensions cap at 128/256; failed results may be negatively cached; factory creation is main-thread/nonblocking while lookup is threadsafe but blocking I/O.
sources.applicability: Implemented desktop analogy and source of alternatives; do not inherit its coarse cache key or use main-thread lookup for latency-sensitive UI.

sources.title: PDF.js RenderTask cancellation API
sources.version_or_commit: Draft documentation; release/version not pinned by this URL
sources.observed_operation: Opened current draft JSDoc; inspected cancellation and promise semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: cancel rejects task promise; if rendering is underway it may wait until graphics pauses with a timeout; API contract does not promise immediate preemption.
sources.applicability: Useful example of cooperative cancellation and asynchronous completion; do not treat cancel request as completion or reuse same output/canvas until terminal.

sources.title: PDF.js DocumentInitParameters defaults
sources.version_or_commit: Draft documentation; release/version not pinned by this URL
sources.locator: DocumentInitParameters, maxImageSize, stopAtErrors, canvasMaxAreaInBytes, progress; lines 63-146, 254-265
sources.observed_operation: Opened current draft API and located documented size/error/progress defaults.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: maxImageSize defaults -1/no limit; stopAtErrors defaults false; canvasMaxAreaInBytes -1 invokes a guess; loading percent is NaN if total is undefined. Defaults depend on browser versus Node for worker/font capabilities.
sources.applicability: Evidence that parser defaults are not job-level resource or reliability limits; configure bounds and support indeterminate progress.

sources.title: PDF.js cancellation history: loadingTask.destroy issue
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue and examined reporter repro, maintainer promise-handling explanation, later user reports, and referenced commits.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Cancellation via destroy before load resolves caused reported Worker was destroyed/terminated errors; maintainer explained rejection handling and closed completed, while subsequent users reported distinct worker errors; commit references appeared in Dec 2025.
sources.applicability: Cancellation needs explicit terminal/error semantics and regression tests; mixed reports distinguish rejected promise from worker error, so do not collapse every complaint into a confirmed library defect.

sources.title: PDF.js cancellation fix commit in community fork
sources.locator: Commit message and src/core/worker.js diff; lines 127-179
sources.observed_operation: Opened immutable commit page linked from issue #11595; reviewed one-file diff.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fix checks terminated state and returns from a second onFailure instead of throwing another uncatchable error; commit is in an individual fork, not evidence of upstream merge.
sources.applicability: Concrete example of making cancellation/failure terminal handling idempotent; preserve upstream-status caveat.

sources.title: PDF.js render teardown issue
sources.version_or_commit: Reported Sep 1 2026; reproduced by reporter on 6.3.289 and 5.7.284
sources.locator: Issue reproduction and suggested fix; lines 130-225, 234-295; status line 140
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue and examined sample, observed promise outcome, proposed finally handling, and status.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reporter says throwing canvas teardown can recur during cancel before callback settles render promise; marked closed as not planned. This is issue evidence, not independently reproduced or accepted as a defect.
sources.applicability: Require every job to settle even when cleanup throws; teardown must not prevent terminal event/reap; regression scenario belongs in validation.

sources.title: PDF.js worker_threads issue and maintainer response
sources.version_or_commit: Reported Sep 11 2026; Windows Node 24, Node worker_threads; versions 5.x tested and 6.0.227/6.3.289
sources.locator: Summary, environment, unchecked scope, maintainer response; lines 130-166, 241-288
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue and inspected sample/version matrix, limitations, and maintainer closure/release response.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reporter claims worker_threads importing 5.x crashes Windows host in one test host; no fault observed in tested 6.x; reporter did not test other Windows machines/Linux Node 24; maintainer says Node worker_threads unsupported, only standard Web Workers supported, and issue was already fixed in latest release.
sources.applicability: A thread shares crash domain with host; isolated process is stronger. Treat exact PDF.js/Node result as scoped report, not universal parser claim.

sources.title: SQLite atomic commit
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation; rollback-journal article, atomicity also supported via separate WAL mechanism
sources.observed_operation: Opened SQLite official article; reviewed atomic transaction meaning and hardware/filesystem assumptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A single transaction appears all-or-none after OS crash or power loss under stated VFS/storage assumptions; article is specifically rollback mode unless paired with WAL documentation.
sources.applicability: If binary preview payload and validity metadata are stored in one DB transaction, avoids split cache commit; cache still evictable and durability settings affect power-loss guarantees.

sources.title: SQLite write-ahead logging
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation; WAL available since SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21)
sources.observed_operation: Opened official WAL documentation; reviewed commit point, concurrency, checkpoint and same-host constraint.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Readers and writer can proceed concurrently, but only one writer exists; shared-memory index requires same machine so WAL does not work over a network filesystem; checkpoints and -wal/-shm state matter.
sources.applicability: Trade-off if cache DB is used; place local and serialize cache writes or choose rollback mode/file cache; do not put WAL DB on network share.
